correctness.rationale: The essential maximum-walk representation is an explicitly attributed published lemma (Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff 2016, Lemma 1). For every oriented edge the stated integer cocycle d_C=3d_H+h(end)-h(start) holds by direct inspection of all color pairs. Since h is restricted to {-2,-1,0}, a nonmaximal GHM path cannot maximize the CCA path weight. The exact rounding H_v(t)=ceil((C_v(t)+h(initial_v))/3) follows for all t including t=0. Event sequence reconstruction gives eventual vertexwise and global period divisibility. Two distinct standalone implementations checked 235653 time/vertex instances and 24142125 finite graph/coloring pairs, respectively. Finite checks alone do not establish the infinite graph-size quantifier.

originality.rationale: Direct inspection of the closest general primary source establishes maximum-walk identities for individual models but not their same-time cross-model rounded count identity or period divisibility from matched initial coloring. The new cocycle and integer maximum separation are extra comparisons, and the event-history reconstruction yields a stronger all-graph outcome than finite joint-period tables. Priority risk remains because the result is a relatively short consequence of an existing strong lemma; this is not claimed as independent certification or exhaustive literature priority.
residual_risks: A publication not identified by the textual or published-finding corpus searches might already state the same cross-model coboundary or period-divisibility theorem.
Because the theorem is derived from a powerful published common input, its first-claim status and significance merit an external subject-matter review.
The asymptotic-activity discussion in the primary paper is not itself a proof of novelty of the exact time-dependent relation.

value.rationale: The exact pointwise coupling connects two classical excitable-media graph dynamical systems from matched initial conditions for every finite simple undirected graph. Unlike isolated finite graph censuses or known asymptotic 3:1 rates, it forbids any nondividing eventual least-period pair on every graph and recovers all GHM excitation events from one CCA counter stream. The observation is structural, not a parameter renaming, and has concrete implications for model comparisons and simulations.
